newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end higher, ignore Dow weakness.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end higher, ignore Dow weakness.

text.p: French shares shrugged off Wall Street's weakness to settle slightly higher on Thursday after fluctuating between negative and positive throughout the day.
Shares pushed higher late in the afternoon and traders said the advance was likely related to the end of the October account. "There were probably some exercises on the option side," said one trader.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 0.13 percent or 2.76 points at 2,151.62 after trading in a narrow 13-point range during the day. The CAC-40 futures contract was up three points at 2,157.0.
Volume totalled 5.18 billion francs with 3.1 billion traded on the CAC-40.

"Trade at the moment is very technical, with shares trading very close to their support and resistance levels," said one trader. "I think it is a fairly healthy pause," he said, adding that his target for the CAC-40 for year-end was 2,250.

Traders said the market should be supported on Friday by buying at the start of the new account. "The market is consolidating an exceptionally good month in volumes we haven't experienced for a very long time," said one trader.

Traders said that the bourse was underpinned by a relatively good first-half earnings season and that even with the French economy showing no signs of shaking off its doldrums, prospects for the market were good.

"We have some really strong earners in the CAC which are not French companies per se like L'Oreal that have a lot of external earnings," said one. "A lot have a heavy dependence on the U.S. which is doing quite well."
* Dassault Systemes ended up 3.24 percent at 216.50 francs after reporting nine-month profits jumped to 209.7 million francs from 117.4 million.
Morgan Stanley reiterated its "neutral" recommendation on Dassault Systemes at the share's current level. The brokerage said it remained confident about the group's outlook for the rest of the year.

* SGS Thomson finished down 0.65 percent at 275.0 francs. Morgan Stanley changed its rating to "strong buy" from "outperform", citing the group's dominant position in most of its activities. It said the share was trading at 12 times its 1997 earnings per share estimate against a sector average of 19 times.
* Rhone-Poulenc closed up 0.85 percent at 142.50 francs. It reports third-quarter earnings on Friday at 0630 GMT.

* Usinor Sacilor ended down 1.03 percent at 76.50 after Transbourse cut its rating from buy to sell saying it feared a five percent fall in special flat steel prices in 1997. It also said it was worried about Usinor's ability to maintain its dividend given its goal of wiping out its debt by end 1997.

* Paribas ended up 1.97 percent at 335.8 francs. A trader cited an interview with chairman Andre Levy-Lang in which he declined to deny rumours about the possible sale of Credit du Nord to Banque Populaire.
* Club Mediterranee ended down 0.64 percent at 326.90 francs after diving nearly 20 percent Wednesday after it warned weak vacation spending would hurt peak season results.
* Credit National ended down 3.65 percent at 227.60 francs amid continued fears about a credit rating downgrade.
* Pathe ended down 3.29 percent at 1,353 francs on the back of News Corp's plans to mortage part of its stake in BSkyB by making a convertible preference share issue.
